title: WAL and ARIES recovery
hook: How does write-ahead logging with ARIES redo and undo recover after a crash?

scenes.caption: Steal and no-force need one rule: log before data.
scenes.narration: Dirty pages may be flushed before commit, called steal, and need not be flushed at commit, called no-force. That works only if the log record reaches disk before the page.

items: STEAL: dirty pages flush early, so UNDO info needed
NO-FORCE: commit only flushes the log, so REDO info needed
Log record hits disk before its page

scenes.caption: Log records carry an LSN; each page remembers the last LSN applied.
scenes.narration: Each log record has an LSN, the transaction ID, a prevLSN chain, and redo and undo data. Each page stores the pageLSN of the last change applied.

elements.text:
LSN | txnId | prevLSN
pageId | undo | redo

page.pageLSN = last LSN
  applied to this page
Checkpoint saves dirty page table and txn table.

scenes.caption: Analysis: scan from the last checkpoint to find dirty pages and losers.
scenes.narration: Recovery starts from the last checkpoint. Analysis scans forward to rebuild the dirty page table and the transaction table, identifying transactions that never committed.

scenes.caption: Redo repeats history for all changes, winners and losers alike.
scenes.narration: Redo starts at the smallest recLSN in the dirty page table and replays records. It skips a change only if the page already has it.

elements.text: Repeating history restores the exact crash state.

scenes.caption: Undo rolls back losers backward via prevLSN, writing compensation records.
scenes.narration: Undo walks each loser transaction backward through prevLSN. Every undo writes a compensation log record, with undoNextLSN, so a crash during recovery never repeats work.

elements.text: CLRs are never undone, so recovery is idempotent.

takeaway: ARIES logs before data, repeats history in redo, then undoes losers using compensation records so recovery survives its own crashes.
